steps.title: Understand principal, rate and time
steps.content: Principal (P) is the amount invested or borrowed. Rate (R) is the annual interest percentage. Time (T) is measured in years unless the question says otherwise.
steps.example: ₹5,000 at 8% per year for 2 years has P=5000, R=8 and T=2.

steps.title: Calculate simple interest
steps.prompt: Find simple interest on ₹2,000 at 5% per year for 3 years.

steps.title: Simple interest formula
steps.content: Simple interest is calculated on the original principal for the whole period. The amount is principal plus simple interest.
steps.example: ₹1,000 at 10% for 2 years gives SI ₹200 and amount ₹1,200.

steps.title: Understand compound interest
steps.prompt: ₹1,000 is compounded annually at 10% for 2 years. What is the final amount?
steps.explanation: After year 1 the amount is ₹1,100. Year 2 interest is 10% of ₹1,100 = ₹110. Final amount = ₹1,210.

steps.title: Compound interest grows on the amount
steps.content: With annual compounding, interest in each year is calculated on the amount after the previous year. For one compounding period per year, Amount = P(1+R/100)^T.
steps.tip: Check whether compounding is annual, half-yearly or quarterly before using the formula.
